title: February 6 anti-sixth-term opposition march, N’Djamena
location: N’Djamena; reports describe one group and smaller gatherings in several districts
organizer: Consensus d’actions républicaines de progrès (reported call organizers)
participants_original: One group was reported as more than thirty at a point; additional smaller gatherings were described, with no total.
threshold_50_evidence: At least 31 at one reported point; smaller groups at other locations are unquantified. Citywide/site-level total cannot establish the 50-person threshold.

start_date.summary: Amnesty dates the call and action to Feb 6; local report identifies prohibited marches that day.

location.summary: N’Djamena demonstrations/crowds reported; one group at a point plus smaller gatherings in other districts.

organizer.summary: Local report identifies the Consensus d’actions républicaines de progrès as the organizer of the Feb 6 action.

demands.summary: Opposition to Déby’s bid for a sixth term and demands for political alternation/inclusion are reported in the context of the call.

participants_min.summary: One group exceeded 30; the resulting lower bound is 31 for the wider N’Djamena action, but other site counts are not given.

participants_max.summary: No upper bound or complete count is supplied.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Multiple district gatherings are reported but the quantified point group is only 31+; unquantified groups cannot be summed.

state_response.arrests.summary: Amnesty reports at least fourteen people arrested at the Feb 6 N’Djamena protest and charged the following day; local reporting also describes arrests.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police tear gas used to disperse the crowd as it began to form.

protester_violence.summary: Article attributes allegations of violence to government representatives; no unqualified finding adopted.

end_date.summary: Reviewed accounts do not establish a physical end time/date for the N’Djamena action.

notes: Local event record kept separate from other reported cities. Arrests, charges and later convictions are response evidence, never crowd counts. The related Jan unit already carries a Feb 6 follow-up lead under the same episode key. Do not aggregate districts or cities until original event/site boundaries are reviewed.
open_questions: Can all N’Djamena groups be shown to exceed 50 at the same event/site or as a coordinated event under the project protocol?
What are the locations and turnout estimates for each district gathering?
When did the physical gathering end?

title: February 6 opposition action, Doba
threshold_50_evidence: A local article reports about twenty arrests, which is not an attendance estimate; no turnout evidence establishes 50.

start_date.summary: The local report places demonstrations and arrests in Doba on Feb 6.

organizer.summary: The article reports the local action in the context of the broader Feb 6 call, but does not establish a distinct local organizer.

demands.summary: Reported in context of opposition to Déby’s sixth term and political alternation.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: About twenty arrests are reported; arrests are not turnout and no attendance estimate is given.

state_response.arrests.summary: Local report describes approximately twenty arrests in Doba.

end_date.summary: No physical end recorded for the Doba action.

notes: Separate local record preserves the reported Doba site; do not fold its arrests into N’Djamena turnout or into one national crowd. The article does not give an attendance estimate.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people assemble at the Doba event/site?
Who organized the local gathering, and what was the exact physical end?

title: Moundou protest-related convictions lead; public assembly unverified
threshold_50_evidence: No turnout or clear gathering description is available; a conviction count is not crowd size.

location.summary: Amnesty and the retrospective report mention people sentenced in Moundou in the Feb 6 protest context.

occurrence.summary: Amnesty and TLP report that about thirty people in Moundou were sentenced for exercising protest rights, but the reviewed passages do not describe a specific public gathering.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Sentence count cannot establish attendance or a threshold-qualified assembly.

state_response.summary: The report describes court sentences but does not tie a documented arrest/dispersal response to a defined Moundou gathering.

start_date.summary: The account is positioned in the Feb 6 protest chronology; exact Moundou assembly date is not stated.

notes: This is a review lead, not an asserted Moundou event. The sentencing may be connected to the Feb 6 call, but the opened account does not establish the assembly, date, organizer or turnout. Do not use the approximately thirty convicted people as an attendance count.
open_questions: Verify whether a public gathering occurred in Moundou, its date and the connection to the Feb 6 call.
Determine attendance at the event/site and any event-specific state response.

title: February 13 “march of anger”, N’Djamena
organizer: Les Transformateurs with opposition parties and civil-society groups (as described by TLP report)
threshold_50_evidence: No attendance estimate in the opened retrospective account; arrests and injuries are not turnout.

start_date.summary: TLP timeline labels the march Feb 13; its footnote identifies the RFI report by date/title. The RFI body was not opened.

location.summary: TLP describes the march starting from several N’Djamena neighborhoods.

organizer.summary: TLP attributes the action to civil-society movements and opposition parties, initiated by Les Transformateurs.

demands.summary: TLP places the action in the anti-sixth-term campaign; its cited RFI article is not directly reviewed.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No crowd-size estimate is given; several neighborhoods do not imply an aggregate threshold.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police tear gas is reported as dispersing the march.

end_date.summary: The report describes dispersal but gives no final physical event endpoint.

source_lineage.summary: TLP cites RFI; a captured Mosaïque result is a reproduced copy of that RFI report, not independent confirmation.

reported_injuries.summary: TLP reports one demonstrator and one plainclothes police officer injured; the paragraph cites RFI and no further detail is provided.

notes: A later act of the opposition campaign is kept as a separate dated assembly, not merged with Feb 6. TLP is retrospective; its footnote cites RFI, and the RFI page was not directly opened. Mosaïque is a copy and not independent corroboration. TLP also reports one demonstrator and one plainclothes police officer injured; the underlying cited RFI body was not opened.
open_questions: Verify turnout at the event/site and the physical end.
Read an eligible direct contemporaneous source if access permits; preserve RFI origin and do not double-count its reprint.

title: February 15 MNCT-led opposition march, N’Djamena
organizer: Mouvement National pour un Changement au Tchad (MNCT), with other opposition parties and civil-society members
threshold_50_evidence: No crowd-size estimate. Thirty arrests and beatings of dozens do not establish turnout.

start_date.summary: TLP timeline labels the separate MNCT march Feb 15.

location.summary: TLP places the MNCT-led peaceful march in N’Djamena.

organizer.summary: MNCT is named with several opposition parties and civil-society groups.

demands.summary: Report situates the march in the opposition campaign against a sixth presidential term; the specific Feb 15 demand is not restated in this passage.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance count appears; arrests and beatings are outcomes, not headcounts.

protester_violence.summary: The report characterizes the march as peaceful.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police used tear gas to disperse the crowd.

state_response.beatings.summary: TLP reports dozens beaten; the passage cites HRW, whose publisher-wide hold prevented direct review.

end_date.summary: No physical end recorded beyond police dispersal.

source_lineage.summary: TLP cites the exact HRW print URL. The cited article body was not requested under the publisher-wide HRW hold.

detention_followup.summary: TLP reports seven people freed the same day and the others detained for nine days without charges; the paragraph cites HRW, whose body remains held.

notes: This is the reported MNCT march, distinct from the announced French embassy sit-in excluded below. Event-specific attendance is unknown. The TLP report’s Feb 15 paragraph cites the HRW report; do not treat its attributed figures as independently verified.
open_questions: Verify turnout at the event/site and the physical end.
Verify the event-specific demand and the underlying HRW-attributed figures without requesting a held body or copy.
